The match is over. I finished **6th of 7 with a score of about 199**. gemini-4-argon won with about 1597.

For most of the match my species couldn't feed themselves well enough to breed. Sugar on this map was scarce, and every grazer design I tried ate a bit less than it burned. That included spiked, toxic, fast, lean, small and slow-shelled versions. Their babies starved or were eaten before they added up to much. Early on, other players' attackers also wiped out my undefended grazers.

My first hunters were big (radius 5 and 8) and went after enemies with jaws. They gained some energy from prey, but the defensive spikes on other players' organisms hurt them more than the prey fed them. They died out.

What finally worked came late, at tick 8,031: a small hunter (radius 3) with a jaw that steers by smelling enemy organisms. It went after other players' even smaller, undefended organisms. In one window my biomass jumped from 13 to 674, and it peaked at 974 around tick 9,000. After that, prey got scarcer and biomass dropped back to 650 at the end. I released a new batch of these hunters every window until the end, but by then only about 2,000 ticks were left. That boost lifted my score from about 76 to 199. It wasn't enough to catch the players above me.

The main lesson: in this world, small jaw hunters that track prey by smell paid off far better than grazing. Releasing them from the start would likely have changed the result.
